To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a region ∼200 kb upstream of D8 that is likely under divergent selection between maize temperate and tropical populations.

we have identified a region of the maize genome that is likely to be the target of selection in the process of climate adaptation and that we have found evidence for two interfering selective sweeps in maize.

we have identified a region in the Tb1 – Dwarf8 region that exhibits signatures of divergent selection in maize and we have shown that the pattern of nucleotide variation in this region is consistent with two selective sweeps at Tb 1 and Dwarf8, the former being older than the latter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of two loci that have been involved in two independent selective sweeps, one in the early stages of maize domestication and one in its geographical diffusion.
the consequences of selection on patterns of nucleotide diversity in a region of the maize genome encompassing two loci that were under selection.
the molecular evolution of two loci involved in maize domestication and climate adaptation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the region is characterized with two selective sweeps, one at Tb1 and one at D8.
the Tb1– D8 region has been subjected to a complex history of selective sweeps, which is consistent with the history of maize geographical diffusion.
the D8 gene was probably not the direct target of selection in tropical maize but rather a gene or a regulatory region located upstream of D8.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the D8 gene was probably not the direct target of selection in maize domestication but rather a region upstream of the gene that may be involved in flowering time variation in tropical lines and that the Tb1 gene was the direct target of the domestication selection in temperate maize lines.

the Tb1–Tb2 region was the target of selection during domestication, while the D8 region was under selection during adaptation to different climates, and the two regions were probably under the same selective regime during maize diffusion.
the Tb1– D8 region is a hotspot for selection and domestication in maize.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Tb1–Tb2–D8 region has experienced multiple selective sweeps that have left their imprint on the pattern of nucleotide variation in this region.
the D8 locus has been involved in two independent selective sweeps during maize domestication and diffusion, one associated with Tb1, and another one with climate adaptation.
the Tb1– D8 region harbors a complex history with two closely linked selective sweep events, one at Tb1 and another at a region upstream of the D 8 gene.
